newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Gloom hangs over regionals.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Gloom hangs over regionals.

text.p: Southeast Asian currencies maintained a weak bias on Monday despite weekend comments by various government officials aimed at calming the market.
Dealers said the dollar continued to be well bid on any signs of weakness after regional currencies hit record lows on Friday on fallout from Indonesia's move to float the rupiah.
But volumes were thin and players showed greater willingness to cash in their gains on the higher end.

In the Philippines, the peso caved in to poor sentiment for the region, falling through the 30 to the U.S. dollar level, last seen when the central bank allowed a de facto devaluation of the currency on July 11.
The peso was quoted at 30.00/20 to the dollar at 0415 GMT against its previous close at 29.80.
Manila traders said the central bank was continuing to stay out of the market and quoting wide bid and offer rates of 27.00/30.15 for the dollar.
The Indonesian rupiah remained under pressure from local dollar demand in a thin market and dealers said it still showed scope to test the 3,000 level.
"Volume is thin. Previously people were trading in (lots of) 10 (million dollars). Now trade volume has shrunk to one or two and sometimes five," a U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said.
The rupiah was quoted at 2,955/65 to the dollar at 0415 GMT, close to its historic low of 2,960 seen on Friday. It opened at 2,875/95.
Jakarta stocks lost over six percent in morning trade with the composite index plunging 42.71 points to 575.00 by 0350 GMT.
Dealers said the market largely ignored President Suharto's comments on Saturday that Indonesia would maintain tight monetary and fiscal policies until the rupiah stabilised.

"There are still a lot of Jakarta corporates who are short of dollars and haven't done enough hedging. The dollar is looking quite well bid at the 2,890 level for the time being," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
Dealers said the money market was also volatile, with overnight money falling to 30 percent from 90 percent and overnight swap to 3.0/4.0 from 7.0/8.0 points.
The Malaysian ringgit traded choppily, rising sharply in early trade on corporate dollar demand before slipping back.
"KL corporates started selling the dollar at the 2.7850 ringgit level this morning and some stop-losses were triggered on the way down," the Singapore dealer said.
The ringgit firmed to 2.75 to the dollar from an opening around 2.78. It was quoted at 2.7745/85 at 0415 GMT.

Dealers said the market showed little reaction to Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's weekend comments that speculators were welcome to hammer down the ringgit as the government was confident of overcoming the crisis.
"The market was a little surprised that nobody was willing to take the dollar higher, so they started selling it off," the dealer said.
The Singapore dollar surrendered early gains and fell back through the 1.51 level to the U.S. dollar in line with the ringgit's decline.

Dealers said the domestic unit was initially supported by Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's comments on Saturday that the Singapore dollar would recover once upheaval in regional currencies had subsided.
In Thailand, the baht weakened towards the key 32 level versus the dollar on spillover jitters and uncertainty over the future of the Thai government after Friday's cabinet reshuffle.
The baht was quoted at 31.90/32.00 to the dollar onshore at 0415 GMT against 31.75/31.85 late on Friday.
Bangkok dealers said the baht's slide was limited by some dollar sales at the resistance level of 32 baht.
"We have not seen any central bank intervention yet this morning. The baht's fall was capped at the 32 level," one said, adding that thin volumes were exaggerating moves.

-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642, Lilian Karunungan in Manila (632-841-8937) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
